mostWorthwhile.text: Making and exporting collagen was the most worthwhile sequence: it connected the repair cell’s internal work to the support built outside it. The picture descriptions made that relationship understandable without assuming detailed knowledge of the pathway.

leastWorthwhile.text: Applying the new fibers was a fairly predictable step after seeing them exported, although it clearly showed the deeper gap being filled.

surprise.text: I expected the edge cells to act directly on the wound; the compatibility feedback showed that local signals came first in this sequence.

arbitrary.text: The need to combine signals with the edge cells first was not obvious to me, though the resulting description gave that action a clear purpose.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested in another chapter that connects cellular work to a visible change in the body, as the collagen and wound-closure sequence did.
